what_it_does: VPIC 2.0 is a plasma simulation code that uses Kokkos (a performance portability abstraction layer) to run efficiently on both CPUs and GPUs. The paper shows how to overcome the overhead typically introduced by such abstractions through three techniques: better vectorization (packing more data operations together), sorting particles in memory layouts optimized for each specific hardware platform, and reorganizing memory access patterns to reduce stalls. This enables the same code to achieve high performance across diverse hardware without custom rewrites.
